anjali: heads-up: saw a sharp throughput/latency cliff on MI300 farm this morning for long sequences (>1024). looks like the selector fell back to a slow generic kernel for a handful of op/block-size combinations.
ryan: can you paste the perf output and the selector log? is this only opset X.Y or more general?
anjali: here are snippets, stripped for brevity. reproduction on prod-sim with a batch of 4, seq=2048.
anjali: ```
perf-summary: model: redwood-v2, hw: mi300, seq:2048, batch:4
- fast_kernel (expected) => 14.2ms/token
- fallback_generic => 48.7ms/token  # ~3.4x slower
kv-stats: hit_rate=0.11, misses spiked when fallback happened
selector-log: WARN no_kernel_match opset=2.3 block=128 dtype=fp16
```
jorge: interesting — two things to check: (1) opset/variant mismatch (we recently onboarded a patched attention op), (2) cached kernel index table might be incomplete after autotuner run.
perf-bot: automated profile attached: latency 35-60ms, higher variance on MI300 nodes with ROCm 6.5. see probe id=prf-1963123456.
ryan: jorge, do we have a quick way to force the selector to prefer an older kernel family (tiled_fp16) when exact block-size match missing?
jorge: currently selector does: exact kernel -> fallback generic -> CPU/slow path. We can add a 'nearest-block-size' preference before the generic path, but need to ensure numeric stability. Also need to ensure cache keys include opset_minor/patch.
anjali: the KV cache hit drop is worrying — looks like when the slow kernel path runs, it increases per-token time enough that concurrent reqs cause more cache evictions (we saw TTL evictions in logs). So routing to another pool might mask but not fix root cause.
sre-bot: suggestion: conditional routing policy: if selector logs WARN no_kernel_match and hw=AMD, then route to dedicated CUDA pool (if available) OR to dedicated AMD pool with autorun autotune job. set a soft limit for that route to avoid overload.
ryan: I'd prefer a local fix first: try nearest-block-size strategy + include opset_patch in kernel keys. patch estimate: ~1d + tests. fallback routing as mitigation.
jorge: agree. I'll prototype selector change. test matrix: block sizes {64,128,256}, seqs {512,1024,2048}, opset {2.2,2.3}. Also add an autotune sweep for missing combos.
anjali: I'll gather traces and KV cache timeline for the 3 incidents today and upload to the issue. we should verify whether kv misses correlate with kernel fallback windows.
perf-bot: note: can reproduce locally with small repro harness: set env ROCM_FORCE_KERN_REMOVAL=1 to simulate missing kernel and measure impact.
ryan: ok owners: ryan -> open patch PR with nearest-block-size heuristic and opset key fix. jorge -> autotune sweep config + smoke tests. anjali -> collect traces and reproduce steps + attach to PR. sre-bot -> add conditional routing runbook if CI reproduces >2x regression.
anjali: thanks. tagging @oncall in case we see customer reports. :thumbsup:
